t: A Hindu-Buddhist kingdom of West Java, ruled in its last century from Pakuan Pajajaran on the site of modern Bogor.
It exported pepper through Sunda Kalapa, the port that became Jakarta, and resisted both Majapahit and the Muslim coastal states.
Banten’s capture of Pakuan in 1579 ended the kingdom, but Sundanese language, literature and identity endure in West Java.
dyk: The stone pillar set up for Sunda’s 1522 treaty with Portugal was rediscovered in Jakarta in 1918 and is now kept in the National Museum of Indonesia.
ev: Traditional date for Tarusbawa’s founding of the kingdom of Sunda
Sanghyang Tapak inscriptions of King Sri Jayabupati
King Linggabuana is killed by Majapahit troops in the Battle of Bubat
Sri Baduga Maharaja unites Sunda and Galuh and rules from Pakuan Pajajaran
Sunda signs a treaty of alliance with the Portuguese of Malacca
Fatahillah’s forces capture Sunda Kalapa, later Jakarta
Surawisesa sets up the Batutulis inscription honouring his father
